How I coach

An hour of exercise is not coaching.

Anyone can make you tired. That is the easy part. What actually changes your body is whether the training progresses week to week, and whether you understand why you are doing it.

So sessions are not random. You get a structure that builds, loads that go up on purpose, and technique fixed on the spot rather than three months and one sore shoulder later.

Nutrition gets built around your actual week, including the Friday. You do not need to give up your weekends to lose fat. You need a plan that survives them.

And you leave knowing the mechanism, not just the exercise. That is the difference between someone who needs a trainer forever and someone who eventually does not.

Injuries do not get avoided, they get worked around properly. I have had my own, including a broken leg that needed surgery, and I have coached people through torn knees, bad backs and joints that could not handle the weight they were carrying. Training around something is not the same as training less. Usually you end up stronger than before it happened.

Where

Personal training at PureGym Giffnock.

This is where the in person work happens. It is a big floor with proper kit, so nothing in your programme is limited by what is free that day.

A session is not me counting your reps at you. We work through the lifts that matter, I fix technique while you are actually doing it, and you leave with the next block already mapped out.

It sits handy for Giffnock, Clarkston, Newton Mearns and the wider Southside, with free parking on site, so it is a short hop rather than a cross city trek after work.

Your coach

I did it the long way round.

I started at 52kg in a gym on Jamaica Street and spent years training four or five times a week with almost nothing to show for it. I tracked everything, read everything, got nowhere.

I took my Level 3 in 2023 while working full time as an analytical scientist, coached a few friends for free in early 2024, and left the lab later that year to do this properly. Over 100 people coached since.

I have also broken myself a fair few times along the way, including a leg that needed surgery, so I have spent years working out how to keep training when something is not right rather than sitting on the couch waiting for it to fix itself.

I know exactly what it feels like to train in this city and get nowhere. That is the bit I fix.

The process

What you actually get.

1

Apply. Three questions, two minutes. I read every one and reply myself.

2

We talk. Your training history, your injuries, your week. Then I tell you straight whether I can help.

3

Sessions plus everything around them. A programme, nutrition that fits your week, and me reviewing it as we go.

The session is the visible bit. What decides the outcome is the other 167 hours, so that is where the rest of the work goes: what you train on the days I do not see you, what you eat around a normal week, and what changes when something stalls.

We work in blocks of 8 to 12 weeks, because that is roughly how long it takes to know whether something is working.
